title: Chicken and Gammon Pie
subtitle: A creamy shortcrust pie with chicken thighs and gammon
excerpt: Tender chicken thigh and chunks of gammon in a thick cream sauce, baked inside a golden shortcrust case. A generous weekend pie that goes well with greens.
sourceNotes: Adapted from British pie-shop tradition for a standard 23cm deep pie dish.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the baked pie whole or in slices. Reheat from frozen at 180C for 30 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling a day ahead and refrigerate. Assemble and bake on the day.

content.text: This is a rich, creamy pie with two kinds of meat. The gammon adds a gentle saltiness that balances the mild chicken. Let the filling cool fully before assembling, so the pastry stays crisp and holds its shape.

items.prepNote: two thirds for the base, one third for the lid

content.text: Melt the butter in the saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft. Add the chicken pieces and cook for 5 minutes until pale gold.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the chicken stock, stirring constantly. Add the thyme and bring to a gentle simmer.

Stir in the double cream and gammon chunks. Simmer gently for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick and the chicken is cooked through. Season with black pepper. Add a little salt only if needed, as the gammon is salty.
Tip the filling onto a tray and leave to cool completely. This is important for a crisp base.
Heat the oven to 200C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry and line the pie dish, leaving a little overhang.
Spoon in the cold filling. Roll the remaining pastry into a lid. Brush the rim with beaten egg, lay the lid on, and press the edges to seal. Trim and crimp.
Cut two slits in the top. Brush all over with beaten egg. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the pastry is deep gold. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The base is pale and soft.
items.cause: The oven was not hot enough or the pie sat on a cold shelf.
items.fix: Place a baking sheet in the oven while it heats up and bake the pie directly on it.

items.symptom: The filling is runny when cut.
items.cause: The sauce was not reduced enough before the pie was assembled.
items.fix: The sauce should coat the back of a spoon thickly before the pie is built. Simmer longer with the lid off.

items.symptom: The lid puffs up and the filling sinks away from it.
items.cause: The slits in the top were too small to let the steam out.
items.fix: Cut two generous slits in the lid before baking so steam can escape freely.
